title: Loops
subject: Computer Science

English.simple_explanation: A loop tells a computer to repeat a set of steps, instead of you writing those steps out again and again.
English.detailed_explanation:
Repetition is where computers are genuinely better than people, and a loop is how you ask for it. Rather than writing an instruction a thousand times, you write it once and say how many times to run it.

There are two shapes. A counting loop runs a known number of times: repeat this ten times. A conditional loop runs until something becomes true: keep going while there is still water in the bucket. Use the first when you know the count in advance and the second when you do not.

Every loop needs a way to stop. A counting loop stops when it reaches its number. A conditional loop stops when its condition changes — which means something inside the loop must eventually change it. If nothing does, the loop runs forever. That is an infinite loop, and it is the classic beginner's bug: not a mistake in any single step, but a missing change.

Loops matter beyond saving typing. A loop written once works for ten items or ten million, so the same short piece of code handles a problem of any size.

real_world_use: checking every file in a folder
common_misconceptions: A loop makes the computer run faster.
A loop always repeats a fixed number of times.
An infinite loop happens because one of the steps inside it is wrong.

observe_around_you.invitation: You need paper, a pen, and one other person.
observe_around_you.what_to_do: Pick a repetitive everyday task — filling a bucket mug by mug, or laying out plates for a meal. First write the instructions with every single repetition spelled out. Then rewrite them using the word repeat and a number or a condition. Give the second version to the other person and see if they can follow it.
observe_around_you.what_to_notice: Compare how long the two versions are. Then ask what has to change if the bucket is twice as big: how much of each version do you have to rewrite?
observe_around_you.concept_link: The spelled-out version has to be rewritten for every new size. The loop version does not change at all — only the number or the condition does. That is the real power of a loop: it separates the instruction from how many times it runs.

think_question: A program says: while the bucket is not full, pour in one mug of water. Someone writes it but forgets to actually pour. What happens, and why is this not a mistake in any single instruction?

reasoning_guide.correct_feedback: Good reasoning: you saw that the condition never changes, so the loop never ends.
reasoning_guide.partial_feedback: You have started well. Say what has to change for the loop to stop, and whether anything in the loop changes it.
reasoning_guide.misconception_feedback: Each instruction may be perfectly correct on its own. The bug is that nothing inside the loop changes the thing the condition is testing, so it stays true forever.

challenge.question: Write instructions using a loop to print the numbers 1 to 5. Say clearly what starts the loop, what stops it, and what changes each time round.
challenge.hint: You need a number that begins somewhere and increases.
progressive_hints: You need a number that begins somewhere and increases.
Start at 1, and stop once you pass 5.
Each time round: print the number, then add 1 to it.
challenge.solution: Set a number to 1. While the number is 5 or less: print the number, then add 1 to it. It starts at 1, it stops when the number becomes 6, and the number increases by 1 each time round — that increase is what eventually stops it.

quiz_questions.question: What is the main purpose of a loop?
options: To repeat steps without writing them out each time
To make the computer run faster
To fix mistakes in a program
correct_answers: To repeat steps without writing them out each time
quiz_questions.explanation: A loop expresses repetition once, instead of the same instruction being written over and over.
quiz_questions.hint: Think about what you avoid having to write.
progressive_hints: Think about what you avoid having to write.
It is about expressing repetition, not about speed.

quiz_questions.question: A loop runs forever and never stops. What is the most likely reason?
options: Nothing inside the loop changes what the condition is testing
The loop has too many steps in it
Loops always have to be stopped by hand
correct_answers: Nothing inside the loop changes what the condition is testing
quiz_questions.explanation: A conditional loop ends when its condition becomes false. If nothing inside ever changes that, it cannot end.
quiz_questions.hint: Ask what would have to change for the loop to stop.
progressive_hints: Ask what would have to change for the loop to stop.
Then ask whether anything inside the loop actually changes it.

quiz_questions.question: You want to read every line of a file, but you do not know how many lines it has. Which kind of loop fits?
options: A counting loop with a fixed number
A conditional loop that runs until the lines run out
A loop that runs exactly once
correct_answers: A conditional loop that runs until the lines run out
quiz_questions.explanation: You cannot count in advance, so the loop must be driven by a condition rather than a number.
quiz_questions.hint: Do you know the number of repetitions before you start?
progressive_hints: Do you know the number of repetitions before you start?
If you cannot know the count, the loop must test something instead.

sources: Standard introductory computer science: counting and conditional loops, loop termination, and infinite loops. Academic review is still needed.
